title: Daring Discovery cast at Zada with three Goblins out

you: Goblin token 1 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Goblin token 2 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Goblin token 3 (1/1 red Goblin creature token)
Mountain x5 (all tapped to cast Daring Discovery)

scenario.mana_available: {0} (the {4}{R} to cast Daring Discovery is already paid; no other mana source)

stack.note: cast with exactly one target, Zada, Hedron Grinder

extras.timing: It is your precombat main phase, you are the active player, and the stack was empty when you cast Daring Discovery (cost {4}{R}, already paid). It has just become cast and is on the stack; any abilities that triggered on casting it have not yet been put on the stack.

scenario.question: Daring Discovery has 'up to three target creatures' and is cast with Zada as its only target. Does Zada's trigger fire, and if so how many copies are created? Does each copy perform its own discover 4, and are the cards cast via discover from those copies themselves 'cast' (so able to trigger Zada again if they target only Zada)?

steps.action: Daring Discovery was cast ({4}{R}, paid by tapping all five Mountains) announcing ONE target for 'up to three target creatures': Zada, Hedron Grinder.
steps.effect: 'Up to three' is a variable number of targets; you announce the number (one) before the target. The spell is targeted, since one target was chosen. The total cost was paid in full; the scenario gives no other mana source, so your pool is empty at the moment the spell is cast (this can change later if a discovered spell adds mana - see step 7 and final_state).

steps.action: Daring Discovery becomes cast; Zada's ability checks its condition.
steps.effect: Daring Discovery is a sorcery spell, and the number of different objects chosen as its targets is one: Zada. So it 'targets only Zada' and Zada's ability TRIGGERS. (Zada's official ruling says the same: it triggers on a spell that targets only Zada and no other object or player.)

steps.effect: Stack, bottom to top: Daring Discovery (targeting Zada), Zada trigger.

steps.action: All players pass; Zada's trigger resolves.
steps.effect: Zada's text copies Daring Discovery once for each OTHER creature you control that the spell could target. Copy-for-each-'could target' effects put each copy on the stack with its own one of those targets, in the order you choose; Daring Discovery has a single chosen target, so each copy gets one. The board has three Goblin creature tokens (1/1 red, no stated targeting restriction), so THREE copies are created, one targeting each Goblin. The copies are put on the stack, not cast, so Zada does NOT trigger off them (Zada's official ruling agrees). Each copy keeps the original's other copiable characteristics, including its discover 4. All copies sit above the original, which resolves last.

Each time an object is put on the stack, it’s put on top of all objects already there.

steps.action: Priority round: no state-based actions, no triggers waiting; you receive priority and all players pass.
steps.effect: Stack, bottom to top: Daring Discovery (Zada), Copy A (Goblin 1), Copy B (Goblin 2), Copy C (Goblin 3) - order as you chose.

citations.quote: The active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves.
If all players pass in succession (that is, if all players pass without taking any actions in between passing), the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves

steps.action: Copy C resolves: its target Goblin is checked (still legal), then its instructions are followed in order.
steps.effect: That Goblin token can't block this turn. Then the copy performs ITS OWN discover 4: exile from the top of your library until a nonland card with mana value 4 or less is exiled; you may cast it without paying its mana cost, otherwise it goes to your hand; the rest go to the bottom in a random order. What is found depends on the unknown library order - this scenario does not specify it.

citations.quote: If the spell or ability specifies targets, it checks whether the targets are still legal.
The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.

“Discover N” means “Exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card with mana value N or less. You may cast that card without paying its mana cost if the resulting spell’s mana value is less than or equal to N. If you don’t cast it, put that card into your hand.

steps.action: If you choose to cast the discovered card, it is CAST during Copy C's resolution.
steps.effect: Casting via discover is a real cast (only the mana cost is waived as an alternative cost), following the full casting procedure including choosing targets, except no player gets priority right after. It becomes the topmost object on the stack and the copy finishes resolving. Because it is CAST, 'whenever you cast' abilities trigger - including Zada's, if the discovered card is an instant or sorcery that you cast targeting only Zada (Zada must still be on the battlefield to be a target). Such a Zada trigger waits until a player would next receive priority. If the discovered spell adds mana (the deck runs Seething Song, Battle Hymn and Brightstone Ritual, all mana value 4 or less), that mana goes into your pool and stays there as unspent mana until the current step or phase ends, so it can pay for later casts this phase.

citations.quote: If an effect specifically instructs or allows a player to cast a spell during resolution, they do so by following the steps in rules 601.2a–i, except no player receives priority after it’s cast. steps.effect: If the discovered card was an instant/sorcery targeting only Zada, its Zada trigger resolves first. It copies that spell once per OTHER creature you control that the spell could target AT THAT MOMENT: three Goblins on this board, but more if an earlier discovered spell created creatures (the deck runs Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command and Empty the Warrens, all discoverable at 4). The discovered spell and its copies all resolve before Copy B. If you put the card in hand, or cast a spell that did not target only Zada, no Zada trigger is added.

steps.action: Once everything above it has resolved, Copy B resolves, then Copy A - each exactly as steps 6-9.
steps.effect: Each target Goblin can't block this turn; each copy performs its own discover 4, each discovered card may be cast for free, and each such cast can itself trigger Zada. The copy count for any such later trigger is one per other creature you control that the spell could target when the trigger resolves - NOT bounded at three, because Goblins made by an earlier discovered spell count.

steps.action: The original Daring Discovery resolves last.
steps.effect: Zada (still a legal target) can't block this turn; the original performs the FOURTH discover 4, with the same cast-and-maybe-retrigger options. Then it goes to your graveyard. If Zada had left the battlefield before this point, the original's only target would be illegal and it would not resolve, losing its discover (the official Daring Discovery ruling says the same).

Put the remaining exiled cards on the bottom of your library in a random order.

final_state.summary: INVARIANT (holds whatever the library holds): Zada's trigger fires on Daring Discovery (one target, Zada, means it targets only Zada); it makes exactly THREE copies of Daring Discovery, one per Goblin token; those copies are not cast and do not retrigger Zada. PROVIDED EACH TARGET IS STILL LEGAL WHEN ITS SPELL RESOLVES: Daring Discovery's discover 4 is performed four times (three copies + the original, which resolves last), and Zada and the three Goblin tokens can't block this turn. Each copy and the original has exactly one target, and a spell whose targets are all illegal does not resolve (608.2b; the 2023-11-10 Daring Discovery ruling agrees), so the count is one fewer for each copy (or the original) whose only target is gone by then - e.g. a discovered Skirk Prospector or Goblin Bombardment sacrificing a later copy's Goblin, or a Grapeshot killing it. CONDITIONAL ON THE UNSPECIFIED LIBRARY: which four cards are discovered, whether each is cast or put into hand, and everything that follows from them. Each card cast via discover IS cast, so a discovered instant or sorcery cast targeting only Zada triggers Zada again, copied once per other creature you control that it could target at that moment - more than three if earlier discovered spells made Goblins. Hand size, board, storm count and mana pool all depend on those hits: cantrips (and their Zada copies) draw, token makers add bodies, and rituals add mana that stays in the pool until the step or phase ends (106.4).

PRIOR FINDING FIXED (summary and count field). final_state.summary now marks only the trigger and the 3-copy count as INVARIANT, and makes the four discovers and the can't-block effects conditional on each target staying legal, citing 608.2b and the 2023-11-10 ruling. final_state.you.daring_discovery_discovers_performed is now '4 if every target stays legal...; one fewer for each...'. The examples match cards.json: Skirk Prospector (MV1, 'Sacrifice a Goblin: Add {R}'), Goblin Bombardment (MV2, 'Sacrifice a creature'), Grapeshot (MV2). Each is usable in the priority window before the next copy (117.3b). daring_discovery_copies_from_zada = 3 is correctly invariant: the copies are made when the trigger resolves (707.10d), before any discover.
